name: DFRobot DFR0469 Gravity: I2C SD2405AL RTC module (real time clock with a built-in rechargeable cell)
//: Catalog record written by /spark:research on 2026-09-29 — read, not chosen. Filled ONLY from what was actually read: DFRobot's wiki and product page, the schematic PDF (Altium text layer plus a rendered image), the dimension drawing (rendered image; its text layer holds only pad designators) and the SD2405AL datasheet copy DFRobot host (grepped for the rows cited). A null is a fact nobody has recorded. verified: true = the vendor's own text at the cited URL; read off an image, inferred or computed = false with why_it_matters.
//why_not: A Gravity board around Wave's SD2405AL, whose cell is sealed inside the chip package and which DFRobot say keeps time 5-8 years unpowered; passed over because it is 35.5 x 22 mm against 22.5 x 21, a 2016 design, its 400 kHz I2C is specified at 4.5-5.5 V only, and a sealed rechargeable cell ages with no way to replace it.
//variant: True of the DFR0469 at PCB V1.0 — the drawing's silkscreen reads 'SD2405 RTC Module(V1.0)' and the schematic is V1.0 dated 2016-12-28 (drawn in Altium by HDJ-CD). Two connectors: a Gravity 4-pin socket (SDA SCL GND VCC) and a 5-pin XH2.54 header that adds INT.
//sources: The 'datasheet' DFRobot host is the SD2405AL datasheet 'High Precision RTC module－SD2405AL (V1.00)' (the PDF's own title is 'SD2403APIdatasheetv1.1-en副本', 16 pages), read only for the rows cited below. The library https://github.com/DFRobot/Gravity-I2C-SD2405-RTC-Module is linked from the wiki and was NOT opened. An older wiki slug (wiki.dfrobot.com/Gravity__I2C_SD2405_RTC_Module_SKU__DFR0469) appeared in search results and was not opened.

needs.note: On both connectors. Pulled to the module's VCC by R2 10K on the module.
On both connectors. Pulled to the module's VCC by R1 10K on the module.

On the 5-pin header only, not on the Gravity socket. On the schematic image it runs from the chip's INT pin (11) straight to J1 with no pull-up on the module; the chip datasheet's drive type for INT was not read, and its FOBAT bit 'enables/disables the INT pin during battery backup mode'.

power.note: 'Operation voltage range: 3.3V~5.5V' — but 'Fast (400kHz) I2C Interface (4.5~5.5V)', so at 3.3 V DFRobot do not promise 400 kHz. The pull-ups return to this pin. Decoupled on the module by C2 100nF and C1 10uF.

//pin_order: This record's footprint is the 5-pin XH2.54 header J1, because it is the only connector that carries INT. The schematic (text layer) numbers J1 1..5 and the image wires pin 1 INT, 2 VCC, 3 GND, 4 SCL, 5 SDA; the drawing's silkscreen column reads SDA SCL GND VCC INT top to bottom, so pad 1 (INT) is the BOTTOM pad — image-read, see pad_1_position. The Gravity 4-pin socket P1 is 1 SDA, 2 SCL, 3 GND, 4 VCC (text layer), which is the standard Gravity I2C order.
//footprint: pinrow5 for the XH2.54 header (a 2.54 mm pitch row; 'XH2.54-5pin header x1' is in the shipping list). A host that wants only I2C would instead carry a PH2.0 4-pin Gravity socket (jst_ph_4, order SDA SCL GND VCC) and use the 'Gravity I2C 4-Pin Sensor Cable x1' that ships with it.

body_mm.where: 'Dimension: 35.50 x 22.00(mm)/1.4 x 0.87 inches'; the product page says the same and 'Weight: 6g'; the drawing (image) reads 35.5 and 22
body_mm.note: Drawing (image): Gravity socket on the left edge, the 5-pad column mid-board, the SD2405AL (a 16-pin SOP-sized package) on the right, and two large circles at the right edge 15 mm apart — the mounting holes Z1/Z2, diameter not dimensioned.
body_mm.why_it_matters: every placement is arranged around it

i2c_address.where: Specification: 'I2C Address: 0x32'; the datasheet: 'The slave address of the SD2405AL is defined as 0110010' (= 0x32 seven-bit)
i2c_address.why_it_matters: Does not collide with the DS3231 family's 0x68, so one of each can share a bus.

supply_range_v.where: 'Operation voltage range:3.3V~5.5V'; the datasheet's VDD pin: '3.3V～5.5V'

i2c_fast_mode_supply_v.where: 'Fast (400kHz) I2C Interface(4.5~5.5V)'; the wiki says the same
i2c_fast_mode_supply_v.why_it_matters: At 3.3 V the 400 kHz figure is not promised; run 100 kHz on a 3.3 V host unless the datasheet's timing table says otherwise (not read).

timekeeping_accuracy_ppm.where: 'Accuracy ±5ppm from -40°C to +85°C'; the datasheet says the same

backup_cell.value: rechargeable cell sealed inside the SD2405AL package
backup_cell.where: 'extremely accurate I2c real-time clock(RTC) with crystal compensation, inner chargeable battery'; pin 2 TEST is a 'Testing pin for Voltage of Inner battery'; the chip switches 'between the primary power supply and battery automatically'
backup_cell.why_it_matters: Nothing to buy and nothing to fit — and nothing to replace when it is worn out. The schematic image shows no external cell, holder or VBAT pad on the board.

backup_life_years.where: 'Even there is no external power, it can still work for 5~8 years, 1uA ultra-low power consumption' — the vendor's claim, as written
backup_life_years.why_it_matters: Whether the module outlives its cell: a rechargeable cell's cycle life and whether it is recharged from VDD were NOT read (see cell_recharged_from_vdd).

timekeeping_battery_current_ua.where: 'Low-power:typical 1uA (inner battery, Ta=25°C)'; the datasheet says the same

cell_recharged_from_vdd.where: the datasheet calls the cell 'chargeable' but the charging section was not read
cell_recharged_from_vdd.why_it_matters: If it charges from VDD, the module recovers from every power cut by itself; if not, the 5-8 years is the cell's whole life.

module_has_i2c_pullups.where: text layer: R1 10K, R2 10K from VCC; the image shows R1 on SCL and R2 on SDA
module_has_i2c_pullups.why_it_matters: The FireBeetle 2 ESP32-S3 V1.2+ has no I2C pull-ups of its own, so these are the bus's pull-ups unless another module brings its own.

int_pullup_on_module.where: on the schematic image the chip's INT (pin 11) goes straight to J1 pin 1 with no resistor
int_pullup_on_module.why_it_matters: If INT is open-drain (not read), the host must pull it up itself.

gravity_socket_pin_order.where: P1 pins 1-4 on the text layer: SDA, SCL, GND, VCC; the wiki's pinout says the same for the 'Gravity Interface'

pad_1_position.value: INT is the bottom pad of the 5-pad column mid-board; SDA the top
pad_1_position.where: silkscreen on the drawing image reads SDA SCL GND VCC INT top to bottom, and the schematic image numbers J1 5..1 in that direction; no pad-1 marker is drawn
pad_1_position.why_it_matters: The generator numbers the row from pad 1; reversed, SDA lands on INT's pad.

mounting_holes.value: 2, on the right edge, 15 mm apart
mounting_holes.where: the drawing image dimensions the pair's spacing as 15 (mm); diameter and inset are not dimensioned
mounting_holes.why_it_matters: What a host board or enclosure boss lines up with.

host_requirements: Feed VCC from the logic rail: the module's 10k pull-ups return to it, so it sets the bus's high level. At 3.3 V run the bus at 100 kHz — DFRobot promise 400 kHz only at 4.5-5.5 V.
Add no I2C pull-ups; the module brings 10k on each line.
INT (5-pin header only) has no pull-up on the module; give it one on the host if the chip's INT is open-drain.
Nothing to fit and nothing to replace: the cell is inside the chip. Plan for the whole module to be the wear part.

sourcing.stock: not stated on the page; ships with a Gravity 4-pin cable and an XH2.54 5-pin header
